pitch_detail.notes: The first bolt sits high, so a small optional piece out to the left helps and should be extended. A neat finger-width traverse leads into a slab section that ends at a roomy ledge.
A clear step up in difficulty: delicate, powerful and pumpy with little respite. It ends with two mantles stacked one on the other. Extend the leftmost draw below the bulge.

Sustained crimping on steep face with some air beneath you and several line choices, none of them easy. Where the dike appears, the neighbouring route bears right, so do not drift left; look up and right for the next bolt.
Plates and jugs give the fingers a break. Extend the bolt under the small roof, drop into an undercling at the lip, then pull over on solid incut holds.

A standalone pitch and the sting of the route. Reach high for positive holds on the bulge left of the belay and lay it back to the top, then step left to clip a high first bolt. Bolts lead up and left then back right on steep rock with big moves and delicate feet. A good rest sits below an orange panel; the exposed technical crux comes above it as the angle increases.

The only pitch that takes gear. Walk-off option: downclimb, walk, then scramble the ridge at 5.7. Rappel option: find the anchors at the edge of the formation and descend with a 70 m rope. Belays through the end of pitch 5 are bolted and rappel-ready.

review.changed: Wrote all six pitches with grades and metre lengths converted from feet. Crux flagged on P2 (top grade) and described in P5 notes. No rappel table: the rap is described as one 70 m rope descent, not station by station.

pitch_detail.notes: Technical face and slab climbing. A hand traverse crosses a crystal band, then a seam runs through a concave slab, followed by a puzzling stretch of slab before a good ledge belay.
Move left and stem up to the first bolt. Holds grow bigger and more positive toward the top. Protection is spaced but the movement is secure. Belay at a flat stance on a low-angle ramp.
Follow the ramp with scattered gear until it steepens, clip a few bolts, then work through the roof above using hand-sized, extended gear. The top gives a fine exposed position on the mini-summit.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches with grades and lengths from feet. No rappel table: only a single anchor into the gully behind the summit is mentioned.

pitch_detail.notes: Start just right of the neighbouring route and pull a small bulge on jugs to reach a right-facing crack system. Layback it, clip the bolt where the crack fades, climb the face placing gear as you can, and make one more bolt-protected move to the anchors. The pitch can be mossy.

Step left into the chimney feature around the roof and extend the first couple of bolts. Climb the vertical wall of golden plates past a move or two of difficulty, then drift up and right on jugs to the anchors. A couple of optional finger-size pieces are recommended.
Follow a broken crack system up and left with hand-size gear, reach a bolt, and wander up the face to a crux bulge. A crescent-shaped hold is key for a deadpoint or dyno to the ledge anchor.

Layback up the right side of the pillar through powerful moves, then move to its centre and pull over the top on a crystal jug. Scramble about 30 ft to the anchor above the lip, then walk off up and right to the top of the peak.

review.changed: Wrote all four pitches; pitch names left out. Crux flagged on P3 (route top grade). No rappel table; the descent is a walk-off.

pitch_detail.notes: Slab broken by small ledges, left of the arete above the big gully. It is well protected but has two separate cruxes, finishing with a move from the right onto a small sloping belay ledge. A small cam in a pocket at foot level covers that last move.

Scramble up right of the belay to the base of a left-leaning splitter hand crack. The crux is in the lower half; higher up, face features help. Scramble about 20 ft more to a good belay nook. Two #4 cams may help, though one will do.

Blocky alpine terrain trending left toward the headwall. A better crack system exists by moving left after the tree, ending at the same belay. Belay at a distinct stance at the base of a flared corner beneath the headwall.

Climb the corner, then left onto a ramp to a small angled roof. Place a solid cam under it, step out left around the roof, and follow the crack above, which eases in its second half, to an arete leading to the summit block. A variation exists by going right before the roof up a right-leaning hand crack.

review.changed: Wrote all four pitches. No rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: From just right of the arete's toe, climb flared cracks to a block forming a small roof (#4 size), bear-hug over it, and continue on easier ground along the arete. Trend slightly right to belay on large ledges midway between the arete and the major dihedral.

Climb the block corner and roof to featured lower-angle terrain, aiming for a vertical hand-sized splitter above. The crux is where the crack pinches briefly. Continue to a ramp, go around left, and belay on a ledge left of the arete.

Step right and climb to the right side of the large ear-shaped flake. Boulder through it using finger locks, pull into an alcove, then follow the crack on its left side over a small roof into easier face climbing along the arete to another large ledge.

About 400 ft of arete climbing over three pitches: face sections and discontinuous cracks on the right side, with ledges for comfortable belays. It ends at a rubble-strewn ledge left of the arete, at the base of a finger crack up a vertical panel.

Climb the finger crack and regain the arete, then pull a roof with a hard move in an off-fingers crack and continue up blocky terrain. Belay on an intermediate ledge or run it out with long alpine draws to the sloping summit ledge.

review.changed: Wrote five entries: pitches 1-3, 4-6 as one block (the text gives them combined), and 7. Lengths from feet. Descent not tabled.

pitch_detail.notes: At the far left of the buttress climb a clean, easy diagonal crack, pull a steep move to a big ledge, traverse right, and go up a flared hand crack to the piton anchor. Can be split at ledges.

The triple-roof pitch. Go straight up a good open book, pull a small bulge to a hand crack, then right around a large roof to an alcove. A tricky traverse left, for leader and follower alike, reaches a ledge.

Follow the finger crack up the left-facing dihedral to a ledge. Then a shallow corner that looks blank but takes good gear (skip the poor piton) leads to a steep hand crack on a face and another ledge. Traverse left over loose rock, make an exposed no-feet traverse, and mantle onto a ledge. Can be split at ledges.
Go up a thin left-facing dihedral, cut right up steep hand cracks, and back left into the dihedral. Continue toward the blank-looking summit headwall.
Just below the blank face go left up a dihedral with some face climbing, easy but runout, to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote all five pitches; lengths are the approximate figures stated (~60 m, ~30 m). The text mentions other possible belay splits, not tabled.
review.other_findings: Stored grade is 5.11 A0; the text gives only free grades (top 5.11) and mentions no aid.

pitch_detail.notes: Start in the major crack system just right of the large roof. Stay in the groove to a small pedestal just before it widens into a chimney on the left. Keep two 3 inch pieces, or one 3 and one 4 inch, for the anchor.

Climb the moss-filled chimney on the groove's left side until you can hoist left onto low-angle ground, then tunnel under a chockstone in the main groove. Continue until the groove ends between boulders and belay under the arch on the right. Save at least one 0.75 inch piece for the anchor.
Go up the right side of the arch through large boulders to low-angle terrain and a big grassy ledge.
On the left of the ledge follow a right-facing corner with some face moves, and belay atop the massive block forming the nose of the wall.
Follow a narrow ledge a few feet, then go up right on a large lieback feature, or take the harder crack farther left past bushes. Belay on a pedestal about 50 ft up.
Very easy ground until the angle relaxes well below the summit block. From there it is class 3 on the right side of the block to the top.

review.changed: Wrote all six pitches; no lengths given. Crux on P2 as the top grade. Descent (east to the SW ridge) not tabled.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb the cracks in the corner to a big ledge. It is possible to scramble down right from here to retreat.
Crack in the corner up to a ledge with a bolt anchor.
The corner crack again, to a ledge with a bolt anchor.
Stay in the corner, mantle onto a slab, and climb into the alcove. Traverse out the large exposed chimney to a perch on a chockstone with a bolt anchor.

Stem from the anchor stance through exposed overhanging double cracks. At the next alcove move left through more steep cracks, exit via a big jug to a mantle on a large ledge. A walk-off to the right is possible from this ledge.
Easy fifth class, following the neighbouring route to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote P1-5 with metre lengths as given, and 6-8 combined. No rappel table: only a general retreat by rappelling P2-4 on a 70 m rope is mentioned.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble stepped ledges and corners to the base of the headwall; several ways exist, including the gully far left.

Wander up and right on face around a small arete to a shallow sloped ledge, then up and left into a groove to a stance below a steep splitter. Clip two bolts through high-stepping moves, head left to a small alcove, clip one more bolt and pull a steep move onto the ledge below the main crack.
Boulder moves off the ground with one bolt, then a long steep hand-and-finger crack with a tenuous tips-crack exit that is the crux. The anchor is on a sloping ledge.

Up and left via a juggy crack with awkward protection, continue the crack system and stem as a second crack joins from the left. Follow the double cracks to the base of a steep right-facing corner and build a gear anchor.
Dihedral, then daring moves left around the arete onto the face, a couple of unprotected exposed face moves, back right into the dihedral and onto a comfortable ledge. Rated PG13.
Step left, up a short wide crack to a ledge, then ledges and wider cracks to the descent ledge.
Scramble the ridge to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote P1-6 with lengths and 7-9 combined. Descent mentions rappelling in general only.
review.other_findings: Stored grade is 5.12-, but the hardest pitch the text grades is 5.11+.

pitch_detail.notes: Begin at the far right end of the ledge. Climb a short splitter, traverse right along ledges, make a short smeary step left to the bottom of a 4 inch crack, and belay at its top on a ledge.
A short finger crack in the corner, escaping left onto scoopy holds. Easier climbing leads to a low-angle ridge at fourth class. Belay on a large ledge that wraps around the ridge.

Stay left on the ridge toward a crack-and-flake system leading to a wide crack in a left-facing corner. Climb it over a roof to a large exposed ledge. A large cam (Bofa size) protects this pitch very well.
A short splitter hand crack, then gendarmes and chimney mazes until you are comfortable unroping. Scramble and chimney on to the summit block.

review.changed: Wrote the four roped pitches; the remaining scrambling is not a described pitch. Descent rappel/downclimb not station by station.

pitch_detail.notes: Wander up the corner system to a large ledge.
Either of two crack systems of about equal grade leads to another large ledge.
Again two crack systems of about equal grade lead to a ledge.
Scramble to another ledge with a splitter in the corner, climb it into a chimney, and belay at the Conclavity, a chockstone ledge topping the chimney.
Climb up and out of the Conclavity, then right to corner systems along the ridge.
Follow the ridge to the summit block.

review.changed: Wrote all six pitches; P1 ungraded in the text so no grade given.

pitch_detail.notes: The offwidth/chimney in a crumbly left-facing corner reaches the ramp system but is poor; other crack systems either side (easier on the left, steeper and more direct on the right) are better. Gain a ledge just before the right-leaning ramp.
Climb the corner ramp to the base of a crack on the left wall and belay there.
Up the crack, then traverse left around the arete to an exposed belay.
Continue up and left on stepped ledges to an overhanging hard traverse and a mantle onto the slab. Run up the slab to a belay below a large corner.
Climb the corner, then pop around right to another splitter that reaches the ridge, which leads to the summit.

Just right of the neighbouring route, climb bolts to a left-leaning trough (5.10a). Move left to a stance, then up the arete with a mantle (5.10b) to another stance. Cut up and left to the corner, with gear to a #1 cam, and continue to the anchor.

PG13. From the anchor climb up (easier left, harder right) past a bolt to a seam with thin gear. Reach a shallow corner and step right, stay right up the face, then left to a flake, over a lip to good holds and the ring anchor. Mentally harder than pitch 1.
PG13. Move up right (protection on the west face) to a ledge or horn, go up, left, then up to the slab past two bolts (5.10a). Cut back right past a couple of horizontals to the ring anchor.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches; PG13 noted in notes. No rappel table: descent is the route on one 70 m rope with knotted ends.

pitch_detail.notes: Sculpted granite rails and crystals past eleven bolts, plus a 0.3 cam, to a ledge.

Crack-boulder off the belay to a roof; sling a couple of larger pieces below it and fit small cams in the lip out left. Pumpy three-dimensional climbing follows, with a thin crack protecting it; micro cams on the right hip help. All gear.
Sustained steep dihedral with a pump that does not let up: stem and layback using intermittent thin cracks in the corner and the overhanging right wall. All gear.
Continue up the dihedral through locks, easier than below, to the golden blocky top-out. All gear.

review.changed: Wrote all four pitches. No rappel table: the text gives a count of four rappels but not station-by-station lengths. The route can be done as two long pitches with extra finger-size gear.

pitch_detail.notes: Start from the left and traverse up ledges to a good belay at the foot of steep cracks in orange rock.
Splitter hand crack through a steep bulge. Belay at the top with a #3 and a doubled sling on a horn.
Take the left finger crack through the bulge to reach the ridge.
About 400 ft of easy fifth and fourth class along the ridge, followed by roughly 800 ft of second and third class to the top.

review.changed: Wrote the four described pitches; stored count of 5 not matched by the text, no padding.

pitch_detail.notes: Cracks, a chimney and knobs lead to a chockstone stance inside the chimney.

Up the chimney, over well-fixed chockstones, and up the offwidth. At its top, step out onto the left wall and climb cracks and knobs to a low-angle wide crack or chimney, and belay on a spacious ledge with a young sequoia.
Angle up and right on low-angle features to the next gash right, and follow it to the summit slabs.

review.changed: Wrote three pitches with no grades or lengths (none given).

pitch_detail.notes: Snow climbing in the couloir, possibly with a 15 ft rock step. In big snow years the step is buried and this pitch starts at the next rock band.
Easy mixed climbing through the next rock step to a small steep snowfield below a much larger rock step.

Take the obvious weakness on the left toward a small roof, pass it on the right, and continue up a steep offwidth/chimney to the snowfield above. Full-value wrestling in the top half; this is the crux.
A long snow pitch with a short easy rock step about halfway, ending at a chimney capped by a chockstone.
Thin torquing in cracks right of the chimney, finishing with a mantle onto the snow gully above. Short but thoughtful.
Easy snow climbing to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote six pitches without grades or lengths (none given per pitch). Descent not tabled.
